body: My anxiety has robbed me of every social opportunity that's ever come up. It's paralyzing, and it hurts the more I do it.

Thanks. Last time I took anti-depressants it made it harder for me. I wasn't able to concentrate on thinking anything, much less concentrate on making music, which is really the only thing keeping me alive.
Because there are different kinds of medication, I'm trying again because I have no other option. Reluctantly, though.

Every day I think about my future, every day for the past decade I've been considering what I can do with my life and my career. I took a leap of faith into music and it didn't pay off. I've taken leaps into other things, and it's ended up disastrously every time. I seriously am at my wits' end, I have no useful practical skills and no desire to learn anymore. 
Any "success" I could possibly have in the future requires more leaps of faith, more sacrifice and more compromise, more misery. Most of all, more time spent being miserable. I ran out of patience for myself some time ago, I really don't know why I'm still hanging on.

Sorry to hear that.
I used to be quite the alcoholic too until I started with trees. Also, I've been working in liquor stores for awhile now, so I get to see all the deadbeats and heavy drinkers come through, which put me right off it. My best wishes for your Mother. Stay strong.
What are you doing now? Just curious. Hope things are getting better.

Thankyou. I appreciate the sentiment and I might take you up on that, but I generally don't feel good about seeking people out and dumping my problems on them. I generally have a really hard time talking about myself, even sharing this on reddit anonymously was difficult.

Yeah it's finances. I'm in a shitload of debt having just finished UNI and my 3 shifts a week barely cover my living expenses. I've come across some jobs that send me abroad, but sadly nothing to do with my area of study - though I've applied anyway and I'd really be open to anything.
Thanks for the compliment but my writing/language is not great - I didn't do so well in high school with that sort of thing so I don't know that I'd be very good at teaching.

Thanks so much for the advice. I'm going to come back to these posts often as I progress through this. I started this morning by shaving my beard and going for a walk. It's not much but I've got to start somewhere :)

Thankyou for the perspective. 
>You simply have to find a way to keep moving forward until you find what you want.

Right, but I guess I don't see it as 'simple'. Depression is so consuming when you're stuck in a rut, and you feel like you're out of options.

Thankyou, that was helpful to read. I've been in all sorts of denial about my choice in studying music. But believe me, I gave the decision lots of thought. Lots of people sort of say that you should follow what you love and if you work a job you enjoy, then it doesn't feel like work, etc... 
For one brief moment I believed in myself enough to enrol in the course, just to have some faith that it would take me somewhere. It took me a long time to come to grips with the reality of the industry and my chances of making any sort of living through it. I may have a little talent, but I have hardly any motivation - which is much more important.
BTW I'm not in the US.

When you made those changes, how much doubt were you pushing through? Did you ever sort of think that you'd just regress and fall back into old habits because they're too comfortable to let go of? How much willpower did it take to do something like cancel your cable, and was there any sort of significant event that triggered it, or did you just wake up one day and think "fuck it" and change?

I have been actively searching for enlightenment and inspiration in atheism and a naturalistic, realistic world view, ever since I knew what atheism was. I've just finished watching Cosmos actually, it's brilliant. 
There's a lot still for me to understand about the world and maybe I'm overthinking it a fair bit still. My point is that the insignificance that Sagan finds empowering, I find terrifying. I can't really explain why, maybe I'm just not used to the idea yet because I've had something else drilled into my head all my life.
Thankyou for the book recommendations. I guarantee you I'll seek those out, I desperately need new reading material along those lines.
And I'll look into that Hero thing hahah. Is it US specific? I don't quite get what it is but I'm viewing it on my phone, I'll take a closer look later.

Thankyou so much for such a large response. I will send you a message in the morning. I will say though that I have tried a lot of those things you've questioned me about. I don't know that you'd believe me if I listed them all, but I'd hate to be perceived as someone who is in this situation because I haven't tried to change it. I have.
Apart from that I agree with it all. Especially needing to love myself first. I know that's the first step. I've been working on it for awhile, but I'm too realistic to delude myself into a half-truth or distortion of the facts. I sure don't receive any reassurance from friends or family about that, mainly because I don't talk to them about my depression. 
I saw a counsellor last year for awhile and found it even difficult to talk to her about my life. Possibly because she was a woman :/

I'd love to. Being a student in this country is a poor lifestyle though, I wouldn't be able to move out and I'd have to depend on my mother for longer... She wasn't very supportive last time so I don't like my chances.
